caption: The drawing depicts a single ceramic bowl positioned in the center of the paper, with the rest of the background left blank and unadorned. The bowl has a wide, rounded body and a rim that is irregular and stepped upward in three angular projections, creating a jagged silhouetted edge. The bowl is shaded in brown tones with areas of lighter beige and subtle hints of darker shadow, giving it a sense of three-dimensionality and curvature. Overlaid on the outer surface of the bowl, there are simple decorative geometric designs in black, consisting of lines, spirals, and solid shapes that follow the contours of the rim and descend in a band along the surface. The interior of the bowl is not visible; the view shows only the exterior and its patterns. The overall composition is centered, with the drawing itself framed inside a slightly darker rectangle, set against a larger, lightly yellowed paper with faint staining around the edges.
title: Ceremonial Bowl
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
